summary.text: 白 is the character for “white.” Its early form is treated as a picture, but what it depicts remains disputed: proposals include a thumb and a cooking or measuring vessel.

formation.text: Pictographic: the early graph is treated as a single picture, though its referent is unsettled. One proposal identifies a thumb; another identifies a cooking or measuring vessel, with the middle stroke marking the join between lid and body. Neither account is established as a consensus.

components.text: The early graph is treated as one pictorial form, not as separate components. Competing proposals identify it as a thumb or a vessel; the graph’s original referent is unresolved.

history.text: The curated script-style forms show an early rounded outline with two interior strokes, a bronze-style form with a pointed upper outline and two interior strokes, and a seal-style form with a taller central stroke and divided body. These forms illustrate graphic variation, not a proven sequence of dated inscriptions or a settled origin.
The Shuowen tradition explains the seal form as 入 joined with 二, interpreting 二 as an “yin number.” This is a historical explanation of the graph, not confirmation of its early pictorial origin.

uncertainties.text: The early referent remains disputed. Other proposals include cloth, flame or light, and a face or head; the vessel proposal does not establish the ancient name or pronunciation of the object.

Reported early uses include the color word 白, 伯, and a place name, but their order and first-attestation dates are unresolved. A proposed sound-based borrowing for 伯 lacks an established sound comparison; another account connects 伯 to the thumb’s supposed leading position. The reported use of 白 for “hundred” has no secure semantic link to “white.”
Comparative proposals for the spoken word 白 differ; neither identifies a sound-bearing component in the graph.

developments.text: A proposed account says the graph 白 was reused to write 伯 because the words sounded alike. The available account gives no dated sound comparison to establish the match; a competing explanation connects 伯 to the thumb’s supposed leading position.

limitations.text: The order of early uses and exact first-attestation dates remain unresolved. The proposed borrowing for 伯 does not establish that “white” developed from the depicted object, whose name and pronunciation are also unresolved.
The reported use for “hundred” does not establish a semantic transition from “white.”
The recorded glosses “pure, unblemished” and “bright” have no dated histories connecting them to earlier senses.

overview.text: 白 means “white.” Its early form was pictorial, but the picture’s subject is disputed; the familiar outline does not settle whether it showed a thumb or a vessel.
